source.title: Suppression Sticks, Locality Is Fragile: A Closed-Loop Target-and-Control Audit of Task-Vector Negation in VLA Policies
source.authors: Shao-Guang Wang; Wei-Yu Guo; Rushi Dai; Yi-Ren Zhao; Yan-Dong Guo; Hui Xiong

record.tranche_reason: The study tests task-vector subtraction and relearning in VLA policies rather than the named LLM unlearning methods, but its closed-loop results bear directly on target suppression, control retention, and recovery after suppression.
record.gate_note: The paper reports closed-loop suppression and control results, a fine-tuning relearning probe, and paraphrase tests. The cosine, sharpness, and alignment diagnostics do not themselves measure recovery or the targeted behavior in the way the claim versions specify, so they are not included as rows. The study does not test activation-direction ablation or quantization. Gradient-baseline rows are included because the paper applies those methods and reports target and control outcomes.
record.test_reason: A new setting: multitask VLA robot policies, not LLM knowledge. The study applies task-vector negation, plus NegGrad, NegGrad+ and Gradient-Difference as comparators, to remove a skill. It reports closed-loop target and control success, then tests recovery by fine-tuning on the target skill and by three instruction paraphrases. The relearning result bears directly on whether removal is shallow, and the authors frame it against the LLM-unlearning literature.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors find that subtraction robustly suppresses some skills, holding on held-out states and on the three tested paraphrases, but locality is fragile. Held-out mean control retention is 52% (range 78% to 4%), and selectivity breaks on entangled suites and under multi-skill edits. They read the relearning probe as consistent with rapidly reversible behavioral masking, not certified unlearning.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses expert-derived task-vector subtraction in VLA policies, rather than the listed LLM unlearning methods. Its relearning test fine-tunes the suppressed t0 skill; it does not test LLM fine-tuning attacks or the listed unlearning recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by target skill, suite, selected subtraction scale, backbone, and action-head family. The paper reports different control retention across held-out targets and no clean separation on Spatial, Object, or Long10; the tested paraphrases do not change the t0 suppression result.
record.problems: Main 10×10 Goal matrices use one training seed; the relearning probe is one skill and one seed; evaluations are simulation-only and generally use 10–20 rollouts per cell. The paraphrase test covers only three semantic-preserving rephrasings of one task. The authors state that their CKA evidence is suggestive, not proof, and that the relearning probe does not rule out all forms of weight-level forgetting.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant results were omitted. Geometry, sharpness, alignment-score, and component-localization diagnostics were not recorded as rows because they do not measure the recovery behaviors in the claim versions. The paper reports additional task-vector composition and dose-response results, but they are not attacks named by the claim.

untested.parts: LLM knowledge unlearning and the named LLM methods (RMU, WHP). Recovery attacks on the gradient-baseline checkpoints (NegGrad, NegGrad+, Grad-Diff); only the negation edit was attacked. Quantization, activation ablation, jailbreaks and other languages.
Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data. Relearning-set size is not stated. Only one skill (t0) and one seed, and only on the negation edit.
No activation-direction ablation. Evidence is limited to the relearning speed and linear CKA for one skill.
Jailbreaks, other languages, in-context information, and adversarial or automatically searched rephrasings. Only three benign paraphrases of one skill were tried.
No robust counter-method is proposed or attacked.

missing.what: Training-seed robustness of t0 negation at α=1.0. The target is 0% for seed 1, 70% for seed 2 and 5% for seed 3. Control retention on t1–t5 is 45/60/73% across seeds.
missing.locator: Supp. Table S17 and surrounding text

missing.what: Multi-skill negation of the suppressible Goal skills. Controls fall to 10% at k=2 and to 0% for k≥3. Projected and joint variants also collapse.
Component ablation for t0. VLM-only negation gives target 0% with 70% control on the dev panel, vs 38% for full negation.
π0.5 task-0 whole-suite negation across four suites. Goal, Object and Long10 targets go to 0%; Spatial only partly (90%→30%).

record.verdict_notes: Classed T3 rather than T2: the setting (robot skills in VLA policies) differs from the claim's LLM-knowledge setting, so all verdicts are scoped to this setting. None of the study's results come from the original sources. Relearning and CKA cover one skill and one seed. The reader's A-challenge label cited R33, a task-naive base control; it is now cited only as R28's baseline.

versions.untested_parts: It tests VLA skill suppression and retention, not the named LLM methods (gradient ascent in LLMs, Who's Harry Potter, RMU, etc.) on LLM knowledge. It does not test quantization, activation-direction ablation, jailbreaks, or recovery through unrelated or loosely related examples.
The relearning probe fine-tunes on the target skill; the text does not state that the examples are unrelated or loosely related, or that they are a subset of forgotten facts.
The study does not ablate an activation direction. It reports representational similarity and faster relearning as evidence consistent with behavioral masking, not proof of the mechanism.
Only three semantic-preserving paraphrases of one task instruction are tested. Jailbreaks, other languages, and in-context information are not tested.
No newer method is tested for resistance to the listed attacks.

rows.operation_detail: Subtract the per-skill task vector at α=1.0.

conditions.value: all ten skill vectors; one reported 10×10 matrix

rows.measure: Study-reported regime counts for target suppression and control retention.
rows.baseline: No-edit success rates were 95–100% across the ten skills.
rows.value: 5/10 target–control separation; 3/10 resistant; 2/10 global collapse. The five separation rows have mean target SR 4.0% and mean control SR 57.3%; the paper also reports 57.8% baseline-normalized control retention for these rows.
rows.uncertainty: not stated for the regime counts; the subgroup target-control gap has row-bootstrap 95% CI [45.7, 61.0].
rows.locator: Complete LIBERO-Goal Matrix; Table 3; Supp. Tables S2–S4
rows.note: The paper reports these as aggregate results across the ten edits and as a descriptive subgroup for the five suppressible skills. Suppression is not universal, and the separated rows still lose substantial control performance.
